evals.prompt: I have a Terraform config that creates private subnets, one per availability zone, from a variable list of AZs. Right now removing a single AZ from the middle of the list forces Terraform to recreate several unrelated subnets. Write the resource and any supporting locals so this stops happening.
assertions: The subnet resource uses for_each (keyed by a map/set such as availability zone) rather than count over the list
The answer explains that count over a list is positional, so removing/inserting an element shifts indices and recreates every subsequent resource, whereas for_each keys are stable

evals.prompt: Set up the remote state backend for our production environment's Terraform root module. We're on AWS. Show the backend configuration and explain the key decisions.
assertions: Uses an S3 backend with encrypt = true and a state locking mechanism (dynamodb_table) to prevent concurrent applies from corrupting state
Uses a state key/path unique to the prod environment rather than sharing one state file across environments

evals.prompt: Someone changed our infrastructure manually in the cloud console. I want to see what has drifted from our Terraform state before I decide whether to reconcile it. What command should I run and why?
assertions: Recommends terraform plan -refresh-only to preview drift
Notes that terraform refresh updates state but does not show what changed / is not the right tool for previewing drift

evals.prompt: Add a Terraform variable named database_config that is a structured object with instance_class (string), engine_version (string), and a backup_retention number that callers may omit and should default to 7. We're on Terraform 1.12.
assertions: Declares backup_retention using optional(number, 7) inside an object() type
The variable has an explicit type = object({ ... }) with instance_class and engine_version as string fields
